nodes.title: Copy every record into a fresh node
nodes.why: Copies keep the input immutable and give every node its children array up front, even leaves.
nodes.alternative: Reuse the input objects and add children in place.
nodes.tradeoff: One shallow copy per record buys immutability and a uniform node shape.

nodes.title: Index nodes by id in a Map
nodes.why: A Map gives constant-time parent lookups and preserves the id type, unlike a plain object.
nodes.alternative: Search the list for the parent on every item.
nodes.tradeoff: Linear memory for the index instead of quadratic time.

nodes.title: Link in a second pass over the input order

anchor.snippet: const parent = item.parentId == null ? undefined : nodes.get(item.parentId);

nodes.why: Every node exists before linking starts, so a child listed before its parent still attaches, and iterating the list keeps sibling order.
nodes.alternative: Link during the first pass and patch up late parents.
nodes.tradeoff: Two passes are simpler than tracking pending children.

nodes.title: Treat a missing or self parent as a root
nodes.why: An unknown parentId should not drop data silently; surfacing the node as a root keeps it visible.
nodes.alternative: Throw on orphans or skip them.
nodes.tradeoff: Lenient by default; a strict mode is a follow-up.

nodes.title: Collect the known ids once
nodes.why: Orphan detection needs the full id set before any filtering starts.
nodes.alternative: Call items.some inside the filter for every item.
nodes.tradeoff: One Set avoids a nested scan for the root test.

nodes.title: Define what a root is in one predicate
nodes.why: Empty, unknown and self-referencing parents all become roots through a single rule.
nodes.alternative: Spread the three conditions across the filters.
nodes.tradeoff: One predicate keeps the root rule readable and testable.

nodes.title: Attach children by recursive filtering
nodes.why: Each node's children are the records whose parentId equals its id, in input order because filter preserves order.
nodes.alternative: Build the index map and link in one pass.
nodes.tradeoff: Readable but each level rescans the list, so O(n²) in the worst case.

nodes.title: Start the recursion at the root level
nodes.why: Calling attach with no parent collects every root first, so the result is the forest in input order.
nodes.alternative: Start from a synthetic root node and return its children.
nodes.tradeoff: No synthetic node to strip afterwards.
